title: Permanence under a lisse tensor
statement:
Let $X$ be smooth of pure
dimension $d$, let $K\in D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ and let
$\mathcal L$ be lisse
of finite rank. Then

$$
K\in{}^pD^{\le0}(X)\ \Longrightarrow\
K\otimes^L\mathcal L\in{}^pD^{\le0}(X),
\qquad
K\in{}^pD^{\ge0}(X)\ \Longrightarrow\
K\otimes^L\mathcal L\in{}^pD^{\ge0}(X),
$$

and the analogous assertions hold for the shifted subcategories.

proof.text:
Use the adic $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ category specified in [def-per-support-condition], with lisse sheaves in [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. Apply [lem-per-adic-lisse-cohomology-calculus] to $K$ and $\mathcal L$. It gives $K\otimes^L\mathcal L\in D^b_c$ and, for every integer $a$ and geometric point $\bar x$, the isomorphism
$$\mathcal H^a(K\otimes^L\mathcal L)_{\bar x}\cong\mathcal H^a(K)_{\bar x}\otimes_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}\mathcal L_{\bar x}.$$
The scheme hypotheses (noetherian, finite-dimensional, with $\ell$ invertible) are part of the domain of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] already required to interpret $K$. In particular, this application uses the lemma for the completed/rational/common-stage coefficients, not a comparison with discrete etale $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-modules.

source.place: First sentence: the exact lisse tensor and the geometric-point computation.

proof.text:
Suppose $K\in{}^pD^{\le0}(X)$. By [def-per-perverse-subcategories] and [def-per-support-condition], $\dim\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H^{-i}(K)\le i$ for every integer $i$. If $\mathcal H^{-i}(K)_{\bar x}=0$, Step 1 gives $\mathcal H^{-i}(K\otimes^L\mathcal L)_{\bar x}=0$, since $0\otimes V=0$. Thus
$$\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H^{-i}(K\otimes^L\mathcal L)\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H^{-i}(K).$$
This also holds if support is defined as the closure of the nonzero-fibre locus, by taking closures of the inclusion. Every chain of irreducible closed subsets in the smaller closed support is a chain in the larger one, so its dimension is at most that of the larger support; empty support has dimension $-\infty$. The required inequality is therefore inherited for every $i$, proving $K\otimes^L\mathcal L\in{}^pD^{\le0}(X)$. Only containment is used: for rank zero the left-hand support is empty.

source.place: First sentence: pass from the cohomology calculation to every support inequality.

proof.text:
Now suppose $K\in{}^pD^{\ge0}(X)$. By [def-per-perverse-subcategories] and [def-per-support-condition], $\operatorname{SuppCon}(D_XK)$ holds. The dual statement in [lem-per-adic-lisse-cohomology-calculus] gives a lisse finite-rank $\mathcal L^\vee$ in degree zero. The isomorphism of [lem-per-dual-lisse-tensor] applies because $X$ is smooth of pure dimension $d$, $K$ is bounded constructible and $\mathcal L$ is lisse finite rank; it identifies
$$D_X(K\otimes^L\mathcal L)\cong D_XK\otimes^L\mathcal L^\vee.$$
Apply Steps 1 and 2 to $D_XK$ and $\mathcal L^\vee$ in the same bounded constructible Verdier-dual setting of [def-per-support-condition]. They give $\operatorname{SuppCon}(D_XK\otimes^L\mathcal L^\vee)$. Isomorphic complexes have isomorphic cohomology and the same supports, so the displayed isomorphism gives $\operatorname{SuppCon}(D_X(K\otimes^L\mathcal L))$. By the two definitions this is precisely $K\otimes^L\mathcal L\in{}^pD^{\ge0}(X)$.

source.place: Second sentence: Verdier duality and the already proved support argument for the lisse dual.

proof.text:
Let $n\in\mathbf Z$. By [def-per-perverse-subcategories], $K\in{}^pD^{\le n}$ (respectively ${}^pD^{\ge n}$) exactly when $K[n]\in{}^pD^{\le0}$ (respectively ${}^pD^{\ge0}$). The derived tensor construction of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] gives
$$(K[n])\otimes^L\mathcal L\cong(K\otimes^L\mathcal L)[n].$$
Indeed, on K-flat cochain representatives the degree-$a$ summands on either side are $K^{p+n}\otimes L^q$ with $p+q=a$. Both differentials are $(-1)^n d_K\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_L$, so the identity on these summands is a chain isomorphism. The same comparison holds after the completed integral construction, scalar localization and passage to a common finite field, which define these operations. Apply Step 2 or Step 3 to $K[n]$ and transport through this isomorphism. The two shifted assertions follow for every $n$.
